question: A car wash handed out loyalty cards: 8 stamps needed, none filled, or 10 needed with 2 already filled. Which got completed more?
answer: The 10-stamp card: 34% of its holders finished, against 19% with the 8-stamp card. Both needed exactly eight washes. Starting a fifth of the way along made the goal feel already under way, and people hurried to finish. Two free stamps on a piece of card bought many extra washes.
move: Notice when a head start was handed to you to keep you going.
ask: Which loyalty card or streak keeps me buying because I'm already partway there?
trap: Reasoning that eight washes needed is eight washes, so equal.
source: Nunes and Drèze, Journal of Consumer Research, 2006
reference: Nunes & Drèze, The Endowed Progress Effect: How Artificial Advancement Increases Effort, Journal of Consumer Research, 2006
